module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1187

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1187](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1187)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [GrTa08] Green, Ben and Tao, Terence, *The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic
  progressions*. Ann. of Math. (2) (2008), 481-547.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1187

/--
Let $k\geq 3$. Is it true that, in any finite colouring of the integers, there are monochromatic
arithmetic progressions of primes of length $k$?

It follows from the theorem of Green and Tao [GrTa08] (that any set of primes with positive
relative density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions) that the answer to the first
question is yes for any $k\geq 3$.

See also [219](https://www.erdosproblems.com/219).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1187.lean#L246"]
theorem erdos_1187.parts.i : answer(True) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    ∀ (κ : Type) [Finite κ] (c : ℤ → κ), ∃ S : Set ℤ, S.IsAPOfLength k ∧
      (∀ n ∈ S, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ (p : ℤ) = n) ∧
        ∃ γ : κ, ∀ n ∈ S, c n = γ := by
  sorry

/--
Let $k\geq 3$. In any finite colouring of the integers, are there monochromatic arithmetic
progressions of length $k$ whose common difference is a prime?

The answer to the second question is trivially no: colouring the integers by their residue modulo
$4$ creates a colouring in which there is not even any monochromatic pair of integers whose
difference is a prime. Alternatively, one can just use $2$ colours and avoid any $3$-term
progressions whose difference is a prime by colouring $0,1\pmod{4}$ red and $2,3\pmod{4}$ blue.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1187.lean#L246"]
theorem erdos_1187.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    ∀ (κ : Type) [Finite κ] (c : ℤ → κ), ∃ (a : ℤ) (p : ℕ) (S : Set ℤ), p.Prime ∧
      S.IsAPOfLengthWith k a p ∧ ∃ γ : κ, ∀ n ∈ S, c n = γ := by
  sorry

end Erdos1187

could_not_verify: Erdos1187.erdos_1187.parts.i — only its formal_proof record is uncertain; the statement's faithfulness is settled. The linked plby theorem `erdos_1187` (L246) implies this declaration, which I proved in Lean from the linked definitions using only standard axioms. But its proof of part (i) imports plby's own Green–Tao formalization (`Wikipedia.GreenTao`, a large transference/Szemerédi development). I could not build that project or run `#print axioms` on it. I spot-checked 6 of its files and found no `sorry` or axiom declarations, which does not cover the whole chain. The part (ii) half of the link is elementary, and I proved part (ii) directly myself.
review.notes:
No misformalizations found. Verification:
(1) Source text. The site page (Wayback, 24 Aug 2026), its LaTeX source and the original [Er80, p.93] all agree. Erdős's wording: "Consider the hypergraph whose vertices are the integers and whose edges are the k term arithmetic progressions. This hypergraph has chromatic number infinity. Does this remain true if we restrict ourselves to arithmetic progressions whose difference is a prime number or all whose terms are primes?" The site's two questions match this, and so do the file's parts (i) and (ii).
(2) Part (i). `S.IsAPOfLength ↑k` includes `ENat.card S = k`, so a constant progression is excluded. I checked in Lean that `{5}` fails and `{3,5,7}` satisfies `IsAPOfLengthWith 3 3 2`. The terms are positive primes, `S` is monochromatic, and the colouring is any `c : ℤ → κ` with `κ : Type` finite, which loses nothing. `answer(True)` matches "yes for any k ≥ 3" (Green–Tao).
(3) Part (ii). I proved `type_of% @erdos_1187.parts.ii` in Lean with the mod-4 colouring, using only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. So `answer(False)` is correct, and the statement still pins down the answer (with `answer(True)` it would be false). Restricting the difference to positive `p : ℕ` loses nothing, since a progression with difference −p is the same set.
(4) Quantifier scope. Part (ii) places `∀ k ≥ 3` inside the answer slot, so `answer(False)` asserts "not for all k ≥ 3". That is weaker than the source's full answer "no for every k ≥ 3"; the mod-4 colouring even kills 2-term progressions. This is the repository's deliberate convention: the answer linter requires quantifiers inside the slot, and maintainers made exactly this change for Erdős 965 in PR #1958. I therefore do not report it.
(5) Status. `research solved` on both parts matches erdosproblems.com ("SOLVED") and Tao's database (informal_status "solved"). The database's formal_status "unformalized" means no formal proof is recorded there. That is a missing record, not a contradiction of the file's formal_proof link.
